summary: In the still darkness of the hovercraft, only the humans are alive. Trinity calls out to Neo, and his eyes open. Tears pour from her smiling eyes as he reaches up to touch her, and she kisses him in a moment that seems like it might last forever. The scene then fades to black and fades back in on a computer screen, where a cursor beats steadily. A phone rings, is answered, and the screen fills with a trace program. Neo's voice is heard over the phone, addressing an unseen audience within the Matrix. He declares he is done running and hiding, and that whether he is done fighting is up to them. He speaks of changing the world from within, describing the Matrix as a potential chrysalis rather than a cage, and urges listeners to free their minds to find a world of hope and peace. The camera glides through the screen's racing numbers and dives toward a constellation of stars, revealed to be the holes in a phone mouthpiece seen from inside.

what_changes.before: Dead or dormant in the still darkness, with only the humans alive around him.
what_changes.after: Revived and reconnected with Trinity, reaching up to touch her as she kisses him.
what_changes.evidence: His eyes open.  Tears pour from her smiling eyes as he reaches up to touch her.

what_changes.before: A man who used to see only the Matrix's edges, boundaries, rules, controls, leaders and laws.
what_changes.after: Done running and hiding, resolved to change the world from within by freeing minds.
what_changes.evidence: I'm done running.  Done hiding.  Whether I'm done fighting, I suppose, is up to you.

what_changes.before: Seeing only the cage of the Matrix and its limitations.
what_changes.after: Understanding that the Matrix can become a chrysalis, and that freedom comes from changing oneself.
what_changes.evidence: That to be free, you cannot change your cage.  You have to change yourself.

event_hint.one_line: Neo revives and reunites with Trinity, then broadcasts a message of liberation to the Matrix.

uncertain: Whether Trinity speaks any lines beyond calling Neo's name, as only 'Neo?' is shown as her dialogue.
The exact nature of the audience Neo addresses within the Matrix.
Whether the kiss scene and the phone call occur in the same continuous moment or represent a transition.

minds.wants: To pull Neo back across the threshold — to make his return real and keep it, after she has already lost him once.
minds.feels: A collision of grief that has not finished and relief that has not yet been trusted. She is holding a man she believes she was promised and then believes she lost; the feeling is too large to be contained in words, so it comes out as tears and a kiss.
minds.shows: Only the call of his name, then silent weeping through a smile as he wakes. She lets everything be seen — there is no guard left here, no crew to perform for; the darkness and the near-loss have stripped her of the contained operative.
minds.basis: She calls 'Neo?' — a question, not a statement, which reads as someone testing whether the return is real rather than declaring it. The tears from smiling eyes and the kiss that 'might last forever' follow the event in which she confessed love over his body and kissed him. The wake has no dialogue for her beyond the name, and that restraint is the residue of someone who has already said the thing she feared would go unheard.

believes_about.belief: That the man waking before her is truly back and not a final flicker she is inventing.
believes_about.wrong_because: Not wrong about his revival — his eyes open and he reaches for her — but the scene gives no assurance that the danger is over; the ship is still breached (sc-221/222), so her certainty that this is a safe reunion is more hope than fact.

minds.wants: To be felt — to close the distance between himself and the others still asleep inside the cage, and to let them know the cage is no longer absolute.
minds.feels: A transformed certainty. He has died and returned, and what he carries out of that is not triumph over the machines but a conviction that the boundary he once saw everywhere — edges, rules, leaders, laws — was a limit he imposed on himself. He is calm, and his calm is the message.
minds.shows: No body, only a voice over a screen; he lets be seen exactly the steadiness of that voice. He withholds the 'how' ('I can't tell you how to get there') and offers only the possibility, which is a deliberate choice — he is inviting, not commanding.
minds.basis: His broadcast reframes the Matrix from cage to chrysalis and locates freedom in changing oneself, directly reversing his earlier line that 'a cage with the door open is still a cage.' The line 'I can feel you now / you can feel me too' mirrors the new reciprocity he has with the world after resurrection. 'I'm done running. Done hiding' answers the whole film's pursuit of him.

believes_about.belief: That deep down they both want this world to change and can feel him now that he stops hiding.
believes_about.wrong_because: Assumed. He has no evidence they want liberation or can even perceive him; he is projecting his own readiness onto a population that has, throughout, been shown to resist waking. The belief is an act of faith, not a reading of them.

connects_back: Trinity's confession and kiss over Neo's dead body (ev-034), which is the emotional source of her tears and the kiss here.
Neo's earlier insistence that a cage with the door open is still a cage (from earlier scenes), now inverted into the chrysalis image.
The sentinel breach at sc-221/222, which is the unresolved physical danger continuing under the tenderness.
The opening phone-and-trace imagery of the film, which this scene deliberately mirrors to close the loop.
sets_up: A Neo who no longer runs, making the proactive assaults of ev-037 (lobby) and the confident escapes of ev-035 psychologically possible.
The public declaration that he can be felt, which sets the machines/Agents to searching for him and raises the stakes of ev-035.
The chrysalis doctrine — that freedom comes from changing oneself — as the thematic ground for everything Neo will attempt from here.
The trace program on screen as the mechanism by which the ship's position can be found, feeding the urgency of ev-035.
dramatic_function: It converts a private resurrection into a public thesis: the scene takes the intimate miracle of Neo's return and reframes it as a doctrine of liberation, closing the film's opening image while opening the world beyond it — moving the story from 'Can he escape the cage?' to 'What happens when the escaped man tells those still inside that the cage was never the real prison?'
